text: the place in the bible that is erroneously  translated as the english word hell is gehenna
and it was an actual physical place of punishment  hey everybody i appreciate and i support this
creator's rhetorical goals but the claims in this  video are not supported by the data there is a
very widespread notion that the references in  the new testament to gehenna are not references
to some spiritual realm of divine punishment but  to the physical location of the valley of hinnom
just to the southwest of the city of david in  jerusalem and that this place was at the time
a landfill where there were perpetually  burning fires where bodies were located where
people were punished none of these ideas are  supported by any archaeological or textual data
from within a thousand years of the composition of  the new testament the earlier earliest reference
of any kind we can find any such idea dates to  around the year 1200 now the references in the new
testament are most likely to a kind of spiritual  divine punishment but there are three different
conceptualizations of this punishment three  different general ideas of how this punishment was
going to be carried out and these ideas developed  in the greco-roman period when that physical
location the valley of hinnom became associated  by figurative extension with postmortem divine
punishment and we have a number of texts that  predate the new testament that date to around the   time of the new testament and that come from after  the new testament that talk about gehenna as a
spiritual location of these three different kinds  of divine punishment one is called annihilationism
that's the idea that the wicked were punished  by simply ceasing to exist upon their death
another was temporary torment or punishment  followed by annihilationism and the third
category is eternal conscious torment the wicked  would go to this place of spiritual punishment to
be punished for eternity all three of these can  be found in different places in the new testament
so the new testament did not have a systematic  consistent conceptualization of the punishment
of the wicked by god following death we find all  three of those things in the new testament but
the notion that gehenna was this physical location  and that this was just places where people would
be punished during life or places where people's  bodies would be thrown after death or where there
were perpetual fires burning none of that is  supported by any archaeological or textual data
and if you'd like to study this on your own i  can recommend two texts for you this is a 2016   book by mark finney called resurrection hell  and the afterlife body and soul in antiquity
judaism and early christianity and this is a  wonderful paper from 2012 called jesus and hell
by heikki räisänen and this comes from the book  jesus in continuum which is an edited volume
